- Overestimate prices in the short term after positive sentiment spikes (especially >0.23), then sharply correct downward.  
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative (especially < -0.16) over recent days.  
- Model tends to overreact to recent price spikes — reduce forecast peak values by 5–10% if sentiment was positive in the prior 3–5 days.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 2–5% unless sentiment is strong bullish.  
- Overshoot after sharp upward moves — cap forecast 3–5 days after a spike at 10–15% below peak if sentiment turns neutral or negative.  
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate early in the window if sentiment is positive; adjust downward by 3–7% for days 1–7 if sentiment >0.15.
